plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to favor income and broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target return of ~1.5%/month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating on income and broad market exposure. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy MSFT, targeting 4% of the book, to add a high-quality tech name from the scanner.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged exposure.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality tech name. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth, blending broad market exposure with strategic tech plays.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, MUU, METU, and SPAL, targeting 7%, 6%, 6%, and 6% respectively, to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Buy MSFT, targeting 6% of the book, to add a high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan stretches for growth by using and adding leveraged ETFs and concentrating in strong setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretch growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, aiming to park cash for yield. It rotates into income-focused ETFs and broad index, cutting high-beta names and leverage. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
